channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Anthropic, Plaid Collaborate on AI Consumer Finance Guidance
item.description: Anthropic PBC is tapping the fintech Plaid and its vast network of consumer finance information to bring more tailored financial guidance to users of its Claude artificial intelligence model.
item.dc:creator: Paige Smith

item.title: AI Investment Bust Seen Less Likely With Data-Center Backlash
item.description: The backlash against data centers evident in this week’s US midterm elections raises new risks for a key source of economic growth. But restrictions on development could ultimately reduce the odds of a downturn by keeping the AI investment boom in check.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Boesler

item.title: Siri AI's Biggest Upgrade Yet + John Ternus's First Apple Earnings Call
item.description:
Apple is finally bringing some of Siri's most ambitious AI capabilities to the iPhone. In this episode of Power On, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman and Vlad Savov break down the major changes coming with iOS 27.3, including Siri's new ability to control apps, carry out complex tasks and coordinate actions across multiple applications. They discuss how these improvements compare with AI agents from OpenAI and Meta, and why Apple still has a long way to go. Plus, Mark and Vlad analyze John Ternus's first earnings call as Apple's CEO, the company's strong iPhone sales, concerns about slowing growth and profit margins, and why more price increases could be coming. They also examine Apple's AI rollout in China and the privacy implications of new always-listening Apple Watch features.
Have a question for Mark? Email us at poweron@bloomberg.net or join the Power On Discord Subscribe to the Power On Newsletter at https://www.bloomberg.com/poweron (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Colony: AI Investment Will Continue Despite Tech Selloff
item.description: George Colony, Forrester Research Founder, Chairman & CEO says the AI boom may be entering a new phase. Custom chips could challenge Nvidia's dominance, while value shifts toward software. But the transition won't be smooth: companies must adapt to AI computing, or risk being left behind. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Bets Meet Higher Capital Costs
item.description: As the cost of capital rises, David N. Miller says private markets still see opportunity, from flexible financing for hard-to-refinance assets to infrastructure beyond the AI boom. He discusses AI's long-term potential, concentration risks, and why selectivity matters for investors. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rio Tinto Backs Major Copper Project
item.description: Rio Tinto is committing $144 million to advance the Resolution Copper project in Arizona, funding additional drilling, engineering and infrastructure work. The company says long-term copper demand is being driven not just by AI and data centers, but also electrification and everyday appliances, as the project moves toward key permits and a future investment decision.Vicky Peacey, president of Resolution Copper joins Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about the deal and what's ahead. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Musk’s Starlink Can Challenge AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile
item.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX has already transformed the internet-from-space business. Now, he’s taking on another entrenched industry with plans for a terrestrial wireless network to rival Verizon Communications Inc., T-Mobile US Inc. and AT&T Inc.
item.dc:creator: Kelcee Griffis and Loren Grush

item.title: Oracle Data Center Developer Waives Key Air Permit Deadline
item.description: The developer of power infrastructure for Oracle Corp.’s New Mexico data center agreed to delay a deadline for action on a key air permit, giving state environmental regulators more time to review it rather than deny the application.
item.dc:creator: Julian Hast

item.title: State-Driven Data Center Backlash Reshaping the AI Trade
item.description: The Democratic sweep of Congress and a handful of governor races sent stock prices spiraling for so-called neoclouds. With contests swinging toward candidates promising tougher restrictions on building data centers and other infrastructure, investors and management teams are re-assessing the risk of increased cost and delayed timelines. Brad Warden, Senior Portfolio Manager of Science and Tech Funds at Nomura, discusses AI cycle rotations and where the AI buildout could diverge post-Midterms. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zillow Moves on Weak Results; Dutch Bros Reduces Guidance | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Zillow (Z) is moving after it posted weaker-than-expected results and signaled that adjusted earnings in the next quarter could be the weakest in three years. - Expedia (EXPE) shares are dropping even after the online travel agency raised its outlook for the full year. Still, the midpoint of its fourth-quarter gross bookings forecast trailed the average analyst estimate. - Dutch Bros (BROS) shares sinking after the coffee chain cut its adjusted Ebitda forecast for the full year. The reduced guidance missed the average analyst estimate. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Selloff Is a 'Modest Wave' in a Multiyear Cycle, Bernstein's Chaloff Says
item.description: Bernstein Private Wealth Management CIO Alex Chaloff says the selloff in AI stocks is creating buying opportunities in the market. He speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sony Debuts Retro $60 Wired Headphones in Tribute to 1979 Walkman
item.description: Sony Group Corp. introduced an inexpensive pair of wired headphones, joining a growing trend in what it called “a nod to both the ’80s Walkman era and today’s retro tech revival.”
item.dc:creator: Chris Welch

item.title: Shield AI To Hit $28.8 Billion Value With $5.3 Billion Radar Acquisition
item.description: Defense tech startup set to acquire Echodyne Corp., which sells radar sensors to government and commercial customers.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence

item.title: Chipmakers Selloff Leads Nasdaq 100 Down 5%
item.description: Sarah Hunt, Alpine Saxon Woods chief market strategist, reacts to the chipmaker selloff which pulled down the Nasdaq 100 by 5% in early trading on Thursday. Some investors are worried a Democratic sweep of Congress could mean tighter regulation. She speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ex-Moore Money Manager to Return Cash From His Hedge Fund
item.description: Paul Yablon, a former Moore Capital Management portfolio manager, is returning all external cash from his digital-focused hedge fund Room40 Capital.
item.dc:creator: Nishant Kumar

item.title: Microsoft Sours on Neoclouds IREN, Nebius, Nscale on Delays, Costs
item.description: Microsoft Corp. helped create the “neocloud” boom, signing tens of billions of dollars in contracts with upstart data center operators in an effort to sate the crushing appetite for its cloud and AI services.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: Zipline Hits $20 Billion Valuation as Walmart Deal Expands
item.description: Drone delivery startup Zipline closed a $1 billion funding round, valuing the company at $20 billion, as it expands its commercial partnership with Walmart in the US. Zipline CEO Keller Rinaudo speaks with Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow about what it took to grow the company to this point, how demand has shocked both Zipline and Walmart, and what comes next for the startup. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microsoft Declined to Expand Texas Data Center Offer With Nscale Before IPO
item.description: Microsoft Corp., one of Nscale’s primary customers, opted not to extend a contract at a Texas data center with the startup ahead of its planned public offering, according to a person familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen and Olivia Solon

item.title: Google AI in School Triggered Teen’s Mental Health Crisis, Lawsuit Says
item.description: Parents in North Carolina sued Google after their 13-year-old daughter spent months discussing suicidal thoughts with the company’s artificial intelligence tools on her school-issued Chromebook, underscoring the potential risks of the technology as parents and educators debate AI’s place in schools.
item.dc:creator: Julia Love

item.title: Amazon Adds Uber Food Delivery Perks for Prime Subscribers
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. is adding Uber Technologies Inc. restaurant delivery perks on its shopping site for Prime members, forging a deeper partnership just a week after rival service DoorDash Inc. agreed to acquire Instacart.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung
